Hi Samira — great to see the usage file, thanks. Short answer and then a proposed pilot outline below.

Summary: we recommend a staged pilot that combines (A) pilot credits to offset experimentation and (B) an option to convert to a 12-month commitment with a steeper discount. For the technical approach, we typically recommend starting with int8/mixed quantization plus KV prefix caching and a conservative batching window (20–40ms) for latency-sensitive summarization. Int4 can yield further cost reductions but we suggest validating on a held-out fidelity set first.

Proposed 3-month pilot (standard):
- Pilot credits: 100k generation tokens included (applies to Optimize tooling evaluation — batching/kv/quant recommendations)
- Technical scope: up to 2 quant variants tested (int8 + experimental int4) on your staging model, batching policy tuned for 30 qps peaks, KV-prefix cache for repeated document prefixes
- Commercial: no commit required; we can offer an introductory 15% credit on Optimize tooling fees during pilot month 1 (one-time)
- Deliverables: pilot proposal + SOW stub, one engineering runbook for suggested config, weekly sync during pilot

If Nimbus is open to a 12-month reserved conversion after pilot, we can provide a commercial option with commit bands and up to 20% off list on the tooling portion (with tiered thresholds).

Practical caveats:
- Int4: potential for higher regression on hallucination-sensitive prompts; recommend A/B and evaluation harness before production swap.
- Batching: small batching windows reduce latency but raise effective qps and GPU footprint — we'll tune for your latency SLOs.
- KV cache: improves unit cost when inputs share prefixes; requires minor app-side cache keying changes.

I attached a short pilot proposal (pilot_proposal_nimbus.pdf) and linked a HubSpot deal (DEAL-9987123) — happy to hop on a call with procurement and your infra lead. Proposed next step: a 30m sync Thurs or Fri to finalize scope.

Mina / team — quick replies: 

- Commercial: 15% one-time credit for month 1 is fine to approve from deal desk for a pilot. For the 12mo commit/20% path, route to CRO and finance (we can pre-authorize a 10% commit-level discount without exec sign-off).

- Int4: be conservative. For summarization where accuracy and hallucination risk matter, int4 can be risky unless you do per-prompt QA and use an eval harness. My recommendation: allow experimental int4 only behind a gated test (A/B evaluation on N=1k prompts, automatic rollback threshold at 1.5% regression vs baseline). Default to mixed-int8 for pilot production runs.

- Ops: Connor — for 30 qps peak with 20–40ms batching + KV caching, plan for a small burst capacity pool (2–3 GPUs) on Hosted; Dedicated is recommended if they need predictable tail latency at scale. Also suggest canary rollout (10% traffic) for any config that changes quantization or cache keys.

Links: internal benchmark: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1Gx-example-link

Happy to sync if you want to walk through the thresholds.
